title: Prefetch invalidation cascade causing runtime crashloop and sustained 5xx error floor
text:
Prefetch invalidation cascade causing runtime crashloop and sustained 5xx error floor

description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 11:20Z we observed a sustained increase in 502/503 errors for a subset of requests from LumenAI. Impact: customer requests experienced elevated 5xx rate (~18% error rate for the tenant) and long tails on streaming sessions, causing application-level timeouts and customer complaints. Scope: dedicated pool for LumenAI in us-east-1; primarily affects model redwood/gptx-13b. Initial symptom: large number of apigw 502s and downstream runtime restarts correlated with a spike in prefix-prefetch invalidations and subsequent cache miss storm.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Send concurrent streaming requests with overlapping long prefixes to redwood/gptx-13b (simulated by LumenAI workload generator).
2) Trigger a model config sync which causes KV cache eviction on the serving nodes (this happened during a customer model pin update).
3) Observe apigw 502/503 rates and runtime logs for kernel fallback / OOM patterns as cache misses amplify request load.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Simultaneous KV cache invalidations caused a prefetch storm that overloaded serving runtime and caused GPU memory pressure leading to OOMs and restart loops.
Hypothesis 2: HTTP/2 multiplexing + high concurrent streaming sessions amplified connection and buffer pressure at apigw which magnified retries and backpressure into runtime.
Metrics checked: tenant token rates, streaming concurrent sessions, runtime GPU memory utilization, restart counts, apigw upstream error rate. Clear correlation between cache invalidation window (11:20-11:26Z) and surge in restarts and 5xxs.
Repro: We reproduced locally by forcing concurrent cache invalidations while running LumenAI request pattern; observed same crashloop when prefetch queue depth exceeded 2000 concurrent fetch tasks.
Additional finding: Autoscaler safety cooldown prevented immediate additional nodes; combined with prefetch work being CPU/GPU heavy, a hot spot formed on a small set of workers.
Cross-references: See SUP-421999 for a related TLS keepalive saturation event during the same customer rollout window. PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 contains the runtime logging and guard introduced as part of the mitigation.

logs:
apigw: 2026-03-10T11:21:12Z - upstream 10.10.5.22:502 - stream reset; concurrent streams: 920; conn_wait: 48ms
runtime: 2026-03-10T11:21:15Z - GPU0 OOM during kv_cache_repopulate; pid=4821; restarting runtime worker
runtime: 2026-03-10T11:21:17Z - Watchdog: worker restart loop detected (3 restarts in 5s), aborting warmup
autoscaler: 2026-03-10T11:22:00Z - scale up request queued; cooldown prevented immediate burst due to safety policy

comments:
Support (Aisha): Customer reported elevated 502/503s and slow streaming; ticket opened 2026-03-10 11:40Z. Notified SRE and runtime on-call.
SRE (Marco): Initial mitigation applied: temporarily increased dedicated pool burst to +25% and disabled the scheduled model config sweep for the tenant to stop further evictions. Observed immediate drop in 5xx to ~2% within 8 minutes.
Runtime Eng (Leena): Added a temporary guard to reject prefetch tasks when prefetch-queue-depth > 1200 and to prefer lightweight async cache fills. Patch validated on staging and promoted to prod at 2026-03-10T12:10Z.
Customer (LumenAI - ops): Confirmed application recovered; they postponed the model pin change that triggered the invalidation. Asked for follow-up on preventing reoccurrence.
Support (Aisha): Closed loop with Customer Success to schedule a briefing and propose configuration changes (prefetch limits and rollout windows) for Dedicated customers.

resolution:
Mitigation: 1) Temporarily increased dedicated pool capacity for the tenant to absorb load. 2) Disabled the model config sweep for LumenAI to stop further KV invalidations. 3) Deployed runtime guard to throttle prefetch tasks when queue depth exceeds safety threshold. 4) Adjusted apigw connection pool and HTTP/2 settings to reduce per-stream buffer amplification. Outcome: error rate reduced to baseline <1.5% and runtime restart loop stopped. Follow-up: create runbook for coordinated cache invalidation, add autoscaler override path for emergency bursts, and land long-term fixes in runtime to make prefetch memory usage more incremental.

next_steps:
Action 1: Engineering to implement incremental prefetch filling (ticket INT-2047), target ETA 2026-03-31.
Action 2: Ops to add a temporary autoscaler emergency scale policy for Dedicated tenants (runbook update by 2026-03-18).
Action 3: Customer Success to run a hardened rollout plan with LumenAI for future model pin changes (scheduled meeting 2026-03-16).
